security_audit.summary: The static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown fences, tutorial code snippets, placeholder RPC URLs, and environment variable examples. I found no prompt injection, secret exfiltration, unauthorized execution, or malicious intent in SKILL.md. The author should add clearer guidance for placeholders, missing resources, and private key hygiene.

remediation.issue: Secret-handling guidance is implicit in the examples.
remediation.suggestion: Add a short warning to use throwaway wallets, never commit .env files, and avoid production keys in tests.

remediation.issue: Referenced resource and asset files are not included in the package.
remediation.suggestion: Include the referenced files or remove the links so users do not follow missing paths.

remediation.issue: Mainnet RPC examples use placeholder providers.
remediation.suggestion: Mark RPC URLs as placeholders and advise users to pin fork blocks for reproducible tests.

content.user_title: Test Smart Contracts With Hardhat and Foundry
content.value_statement: Smart contract teams need repeatable tests for contracts, DeFi integrations, gas costs, and forked networks. This skill provides testing patterns, setup guidance, and verification workflows for Hardhat and Foundry.
actual_capabilities: Explains Hardhat configuration for Solidity compiler settings, forked networks, gas reporting, coverage, and Etherscan verification.
Provides unit test patterns for deployments, transfers, events, reverts, time changes, and gas checks.
Shows Foundry test patterns with fixtures, prank, deal, fuzzing, and mainnet fork examples.
Covers mainnet fork workflows using Hardhat reset and existing DeFi contract addresses.
Includes CI guidance for compiling, testing, coverage, and Codecov upload.
limitations: It is a guide, not an executable test runner or contract auditor.
Referenced resource and asset files are listed but are not present in this package.
Examples use placeholders and must be adapted to the user project, network, and contract interfaces.
It does not prove economic safety or formal correctness by itself.

use_cases.title: Build a Solidity test suite
use_cases.description: Create coverage for deployment, ownership, token transfers, event emissions, revert paths, and time-based logic.

use_cases.title: Validate DeFi integrations
use_cases.description: Design mainnet fork tests that interact with real protocol contracts and pinned block numbers.

use_cases.title: Add CI coverage checks
use_cases.description: Plan automated compile, test, gas, coverage, and reporting steps for pull requests.

prompt_templates.title: Create a first unit test
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a small contract test suite.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me write beginner Hardhat tests for this Solidity contract. Cover deployment, ownership, transfers, events, and expected reverts.

prompt_templates.title: Add Foundry fuzz coverage
prompt_templates.prompt: Design Foundry tests for this contract. Include setup, prank usage, balance assertions, expected reverts, and fuzz cases for boundary values.

prompt_templates.title: Plan mainnet fork scenarios
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for integration tests against live protocol state.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a mainnet fork testing plan for this DeFi workflow. Include pinned blocks, contract addresses, impersonation needs, and balance assertions.

prompt_templates.title: Review testing strategy
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for test completeness and risk coverage.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my smart contract testing strategy. Identify missing unit, integration, fuzz, fork, gas, access control, and CI coverage.

output_examples.input: A developer asks for Hardhat tests for an ERC20 token.
output_examples.output: A test plan covering deployment, initial balances, transfers, revert cases, events, and gas usage checks.

output_examples.input: A protocol engineer asks for a forked Uniswap integration test.
output_examples.output: A scenario list that resets a mainnet fork, connects to live token contracts, performs swaps, and verifies balances.

output_examples.input: A team asks how to add coverage to CI.
output_examples.output: A workflow outline that compiles contracts, runs tests, generates coverage, and uploads reports.

best_practices: Use fixtures to isolate state and make tests repeatable.
Use mainnet forks only with pinned block numbers and documented RPC configuration.
Keep private keys and API keys outside source control and use test wallets.
anti_patterns: Do not rely only on happy path unit tests for value-moving contracts.
Do not run fork tests against floating latest blocks when results must be reproducible.
Do not place real private keys, RPC keys, or deployment secrets in shared examples.

faq.question: Which frameworks does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers Hardhat and Foundry testing patterns for Solidity smart contracts.

faq.question: Can it help with mainnet fork tests?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains fork setup, pinned blocks, existing contract addresses, and account impersonation patterns.

faq.question: Does this skill audit contract security?
faq.answer: No. It helps design tests, but it does not replace a security audit.

faq.question: Does it require private keys?
faq.answer: Most local tests do not need private keys. Deployment and verification examples should use test wallets and environment variables.

faq.question: Can it support CI pipelines?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for compile, test, coverage, and report upload steps.

faq.question: Can it prove a protocol is economically safe?
faq.answer: No. Tests reduce risk, but economic safety needs deeper modeling, review, and monitoring.
